# Zombies: T5 measured against CoDOL (actor behaviour)

2026-10-21. Real Black Ops (T5) was run and its zombies and hellhounds were
recorded frame by frame. CoDOL was then recorded the same way and brought into
line. Scope: actor behaviour only. Player movement and snapshots are out of
scope. Companion docs: `ZOMBIE_T5_PARITY.md` (script-level audit) and
`ZOMBIE_DOGS_T5_PARITY.md`.

## How T5 was captured

- **Game:** the Steam install (`D:\SteamLibrary\...\Call of Duty Black Ops`),
  run through Plutonium's T5 SP client, which was already on this machine.
  Launch: `plutonium-bootstrapper-win32.exe t5sp "<T5 dir>" -lan +set
  r_fullscreen 0 +set r_mode 800x600 +set t5cap_scn <name> ... +devmap
  zombie_cod5_prototype` (`tools/t5cap/t5run.ps1`). Plutonium runs without
  Steam DRM or VAC. Nothing was injected into the game process.
- **Hook:** a GSC capture script loaded by Plutonium from
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Plutonium\storage\t5\scripts\sp\zz_t5cap.gsc`. The repo
  copy is `tools/t5cap/zz_t5cap.gsc`. It uses Plutonium's `replaceFunc` to
  log each melee clip choice, `fs_fopen`/`fs_writeline` for the log, and
  `cmdExec("quit")` when the run ends.
  - **Every 50 ms, per zombie and hound:** origin, yaw, health, move bucket,
    run cycle, `a.script`, `a.movement`, the playback rates, legs, inside or
    outside, enemy and distance, and goal.
  - **Events:** spawn; every notetrack of `meleeanim`, `tear_anim`,
    `traverseAnim`, `deathanim` and `painanim`; `goal` and `bad_path`;
    traverse start and end; damage; death; and player damage with its
    attacker and distance.
  - **Scenarios (dvars):** round and speed staging, a frozen or scripted
    player path, forced crawlers and hound spawns.
  - **"dump" scenario:** uses `getAnimLength`, `getMoveDelta` and
    `getNotetrackTimes` to read every T5 zombie and hound clip's length,
    root travel, 40-step root-motion profile and fire/end notetracks.
- **CoDOL side:** the same script body with a CoDOL platform block,
  `bin/home/codol_rawfiles/maps/_zombiemode_t5cap.gsc`, regenerated by
  `tools/t5cap/mk.py`. It runs on a probe server (`tools/probe.ps1`,
  udp/17785-17786, own home, `g_difficulty 1`, test client `t5cap_bot 1`).
  The read-only actor field `codolanimscript` supplies the native animscript
  name.
- **Analysis:** `tools/t5cap_analyze.py <log>...`. Raw logs are kept in
  `obj/t5capture/` (gitignored): `t5_*.txt` from T5, `codol_*.txt` from CoDOL
  (`codol_proto_*` before the fixes, `codol_v2_*`/`codol_v3_*` after).

| Scenario | T5 map | CoDOL map | Staging |
|---|---|---|---|
| Round 1 walkers, frozen player | zombie_cod5_prototype | zm_prototype_sh | natural round 1, 180-200 s |
| Runners | prototype | prototype | `zombie_move_speed` 40, round 5 health |
| Sprinters | prototype | prototype | `zombie_move_speed` 75, round 8 health |
| Moving player | prototype | prototype | the player walks (0,400)-(0,-300) at 120 u/s |
| Crawlers | prototype | prototype | every second zombie that gets inside loses a leg (T5 `zombie_gib_on_damage` leg branch) |
| Hounds | zombie_cod5_sumpf | zm_sumpf_sh | six hounds (`special_dog_spawn` / `spawn_dog`) |
| Asylum | zombie_cod5_asylum | zm_asylum_sh | runners, frozen player |

## Results

"Before" is current server main (747fb71b / rawfiles c5e7235). "After" is
this branch. Speeds are 2D u/s on straight 50 ms frames, as median
(p10-p90).

### 1. Movement

| Metric | T5 | CoDOL before | CoDOL after |
|---|---|---|---|
| walk_v1 | 37.7 (36.1-38.6) | 35.6 (8-38) | 36.1 (35.4-37.4) |
| walk_v2 | 38.5 (37.2-40.0) | 28.3 (7-47) | 38.2 (37.2-39.6) |
| walk_v3 | 38.0 (36.0-38.1) | n/a | 37.6 (36.1-38.4) |
| walk_v4 | 47.5 (46.0-48.4) | 27.5 (6-63) | 48.0 (46.5-48.3) |
| walk_v6 | 22.4 (22.0-24.2) | 24.4 (10-42) | 22.8 (21.5-24.1) |
| walk_v9 | 26.1 (24.7-26.9) | 37.4 (34-38) | 26.1 (25.3-26.9) |
| walk_fast_v1 | 58.5 flat, 110 lurch once a cycle | 65.4 flat | 58.8, same lurch |
| walk_fast_v2 / v3 | 80.2 / 78.1 | 80.6 / 78.2 | 80.6 / 78.5 |
| run_v2 | 108.2 | 109.2 | 109.2 |
| run5 slot (T5 run_v4; C1 plays run_v1) | 92.1 (83-104) | 120.1 | 93.0 (86-104) |
| sprint_v1 / v2 | 141.5 / 144.5 | 140.1 / 139.7 | 140.0 / 145.3 |
| crawl1 / crawl2 / crawl5 | 19.7 / 14.6 / 57.7 | 16.1 / 14.1 / 58.0 | 20.0 / 14.1 / 58.0 |
| Turn cap | **220 °/s** (every capped step 11.0° per think) | 300 °/s, spikes to 1348 | 220 °/s |
| Hound trot | 135-136, every hound | 122-149 (rate jittered per hound) | 134-137 |
| Hound turn cap | 220 °/s | 360 °/s | 220 °/s |
| Hound run | 360 flat after a 4-frame ramp | 250-340 | 260-355 (open, see 5) |

**Cause.** T5 moves a pathing actor by its clip's per-frame root motion, and
T5's clips have their own root tracks. Most are flat; walk_fast_v1 has one
lurch per cycle. C1 ships the same clips at the same lengths but different
tracks: some linear, some raw and uneven. walk_v4 runs from 10 to 113 u/s
inside one cycle.

**Fix (native).** `ActorAdvanceGoalAnimation` takes each frame's path
distance from T5's measured track of every weighted move clip.
`src/online/player/actor_t5_root.c` is generated by
`tools/t5_root_table.py` from the T5 dump.
- A clip of a different length (C1's walk_v6 is 5.0 s, T5's 4.2 s) moves at
  its C1 average speed.
- C1's run_v1, standing in for the missing run_v4, walks run_v4's track
  scaled onto its own cycle.
- Branches with no root motion, such as the hound's look and aim
  additives, no longer share weight.
- Turn rate: `ActorOrientToDirection` uses 220 °/s for every species.
- Hound move states play at rate 1 (`ActorStateRate`), as T5's
  `moveplaybackrate`.
- `actorT5Pace 0` restores the C1 per-frame delta.

### 2. Spawning and the entrance

| Metric (Prototype round 1) | T5 | CoDOL before | CoDOL after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spawn points | the far structs: (1808 -1398), (-1324 -1056), (1971 -1155), (-1393 -62) | approach nodes 160-320 units from the window | the far structs |
| Spawn -> first board | 37.6 s (29-49) | 8.5 s (7-10) | 27-44 s |
| Spawn -> inside | 53.5 s (48-79) | 22-25 s | 49-52 s |
| Spawn interval, round 1 | 2.1 s | 2.05 s (`g_difficulty 1`; 2.5 s on tier 0, which is by design) | 2.05 s |
| Board-to-board | 2.7-3.0 s | 3.0 s | 3.0 s |
| Window climb (start -> end traverse) | walk 2.15 s, run 1.8 s, sprint 1.35 s | 1.45-1.6 s | 1.7-1.8 s |
| Zombies that got inside | all | all | all, on all three maps |

**Fixes.**
- **Spawning:** `near_window_spawn` (`scr_zm_spawn_near_window`) is off by
  default. Its premise, that T5 kept spawns near the boards, is contradicted
  by the capture.
- **Traversal:** the traversal clip plays at rate 1, then 0.2 s of run cycle
  before `zombie_end_traverse` (T5 `DoTraverse`).

### 3. Melee

| Metric | T5 | CoDOL before | CoDOL after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hits per zombie-second within 80 u, frozen player, walkers | 0.75 | 0.91-0.96 | 0.77 |
| Interval between hits (median) | 1400 ms | 933-1083 ms | 1350 ms |
| Distance at the hit | 31 (p90 48-54) | 30 (p90 32) | 30 (p90 32-62) |
| Moving player: time in combat | 14 % | 34 % | 14 % |
| Moving player: hits per zombie-second | 0.63 | 1.66 | 0.58 |
| Moving player: distance at the hit | 40.5 | n/a | 41 |
| Damage per hit / hound bite | 60 / 40 | 60 / 40 | 60 / 40 |

The melee clips have the same lengths in T5 and C1, but C1 moved several
`fire` notes. The table gives the hit times as a fraction of the clip
(T5 from `getNotetrackTimes`, C1 from the xanim).

| Clip | T5 hits | C1 hits |
|---|---|---|
| attack_v2 | .097 .325 .534 .623 .744 | .093 .186 .516 .595 .665 |
| attack_v1 | .462 .722 | .204 .574 |
| attack_forward_v1 | .414 .600 | .214 .714 |
| attack_forward_v2 | .26 .42 | .26 .64 |
| walk_attack_v1 | .187 | .344 |
| walk_attack_v2 | .595 | .214 .286 .762 |
| walk_attack_v4 | .431 | .045 .11 .41 |
| attack_v4, attack_v6, walk_attack_v3 | same | same |

**Fixes (GSC).**
- ~~`zombie_combat.gsc` lands each swing's hits at T5's fractions~~
  Reverted 2026-10-25, see "Hit timing follows C1's clips" below.
- A regular zombie no longer sets `safeToChangeScript = false` for the swing.
  T5 holds the swing only with `noChangeDuringMelee` (zombie_melee.gsc
  :117-120). The engine therefore takes a zombie off a swing as soon as the
  player is out of reach.

**Hit timing follows C1's clips (2026-10-25).** The T5 fractions above
describe T5's xanims. The client plays C1's clips, so hits at T5's fractions
landed off the swing the player sees. C1's xanims were measured with
`CodolSoundDumper anim-pose` on `c_zom_ger_body1`, frame by frame, taking
wrist reach ahead of the spine and wrist speed. In 13 of the 17 melee clips
the C1 `fire` notes sit within one frame of a strike (a wrist's peak forward
reach). Those clips hit on their notes again, as T5's zombie_melee.gsc:134
does. The other four get a strike schedule (`_zombiemode.gsc`
`zombie_melee_strike`):

| Clip | C1 `fire` frames | Strike frames used |
|---|---|---|
| attack_v6 (70 frames) | 3, 49 | 15 (left), 32 (right) |
| walk_attack_v2 (42) | 9, 12, 32 | 12, 32 |
| walk_attack_v4 (44) | 2, 5, 18 | 5, 18 |
| run_attack_v3 (28) | none (frame 3 is `fire_spray`) | 3, 19 |

On Prototype probes (`t5cap` with per-swing `Z` lines), player damage was
compared with the nearest strike frame of the clip:

| Run | Hits | Median error | p90 | Within 100 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Walkers, before | 428 | 200 ms | 566 ms | 28 % |
| Walkers, after | 406 | 0 ms | 50 ms | 100 % |
| Sprinters, before | 547 | 200 ms | 566 ms | 23 % |
| Sprinters, after | 623 | 1 ms | 50 ms | 100 % |

The server delivers `fire` notetracks within one frame of the clip's note
time (median 17 ms), so the anim clock and notetrack delivery were never the
cause. `scr_zm_melee_strikes -1` uses the notes for every clip.

### 4. Not comparable or by design

- **Shi No Numa's zombies.** T5 swaps walk5-8, run4-6 and sprint3-4 for the
  WaW Japanese clips (`_waw_zombiemode_ai_japanese`). C1 ships none of them,
  so zm_sumpf_sh keeps the standard cycles.
- **Difficulty tiers 0 and 2** (spawn delay, health) are C1's lobby design.
  Tier 1 equals T5.
- **The CoDOL round-5 boss** (an=zombie, ~23k health) has no T5 counterpart.
  It is excluded from the tables.

### 5. Follow-up pass (2026-10-21, later)

| Metric | T5 | CoDOL before | CoDOL after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hound run, the same staged path (hound at (9800 640), player at (10600 620), zombie_cod5_sumpf / zm_sumpf_sh) | flat 362 after a 4-frame ramp | 290-355 wobble | flat 362 after a 3-frame ramp |
| Distance where the 2nd and 3rd hounds break into the run | 475-482 | never (trotted the whole way) | 486 |
| Crowd nearest-neighbour distance, zombies within 90 of a frozen player | median 33-34 (p10 30) | 28 (p10 26-27) | 32 (p10 31) |
| Board torn to clip end | 1.45 s | 1.38 s | 1.40 s |
| Clip end to next board torn | 1.45 s (p90 1.75) | 1.50 s (p90 1.92) | 1.53 s (p90 1.90) |
| Six boards in total | 15.2-18.3 s | 16.3-18.6 s | 15.3-16.7 s |
| crawl1 / crawl2 / crawl3 / crawl4 / crawl5 (300 s, all crawlers) | 20.0 / 14.1 / 62.0 / 90.4 / 58.0 | n/a | 18.4 / 14.1 / 64.4 / 88.8 / 58.0 |

- **Hound run (native).** C1 marks the hound's look-at additives
  (`zombie_dog_look_up` / `_right`, which sit beside the run knob) as
  delta clips with zero travel. They took 10-17 % of the run's weight in the
  path pace (`ai_tracePace <ent>` prints it per frame). A zero-travel
  delta leaf no longer shares weight.
- **Hound sight (native).** When a zombie-mode actor uses `cansee`, other
  actors' bodies no longer block it. In T5 every hound sees the player over
  the first hound biting him (logged `cs=1`). In CoDOL the 2nd and 3rd saw
  the first hound's body (`cs=0`), so `need_to_run` never fired.
- **Crowd spacing (native).** Hunting zombies are pushed apart to 32. The
  old 28 is kept next to an actor on a scripted clip or still working its
  window (`ignoreall`). With 32 everywhere, zombies were pushed off
  neighbouring attack spots, and the gap to the next board grew to 1.7 s
  (p90 3.0 s).
- **Tear clips by attack spot (GSC).** As in T5 :1785, spot 0 uses the
  middle set, 1 the right and 2 the left; the board position no longer picks
  the set.
- **crawl4.** The earlier 96 against 83 came from 88 frames. With 530
  against 240 frames it is 88.8 against 90.4.
- **Melee range (residual).** The spacing put CoDOL's distance mix at hit
  close to T5's: on Asylum 58/29/5/3/2 % at 24/32/40/48/56 units, against
  T5's 50/22/7/11/7. CoDOL still has fewer hits from 48-56 units (5 % against
  T5's 10-18 %). T5's exposed think swings when the path is exhausted, while
  CoDOL swings within 64 with a clear line. Both give the same entry
  distribution (48-63 on approach), so the remainder is crowd geometry, not
  the trigger.

### 6. Animation trees and the Thundergun (2026-10-21)

- **Cause of the "wrong animations / T-posing zombies" report.** The
  Thundergun port named 16 `%ai_zombie_thundergun_*` clips, and zombie_move
  named `%walk_and_run_loops`. No animlist C1 loads names them on Prototype or
  Asylum, so they entered the server's `generic_human` tree only (server 263
  entries, C1 247). The actor channel sends the server entry index, so every
  clip past entry 231, the walk cycles included, was wrong on C1.
- **Fix.**
  - The clips are looked up with `codol_getAnim`.
  - The native guard (`model_animation.c`) logs and refuses, at script
    load, any server anim name that no C1 animlist carries.
  - The server logs each map animlist's entries at load.
- **Knockdown on maps without T5's clips.** Prototype, Asylum and Training
  ship no fall or getup clip at all. C1's own clips stand in:
  - `ai_zombie_humangun_react` (a 1.33 s stagger) for the fall;
  - `ai_zombie_walk_on_hands_shot_a/b` for a crawler;
  - `ai_zombie_flash_react_01` (a daze) for the getup, played at T5's ~3 s.
- **Knockdown on Shi No Numa.** zm_sumpf_sh's own animlist (48 entries)
  ships most of T5's Thundergun set, so Sumpf plays the T5 clips. The three
  it lacks fall back to a sibling clip (forwardtoface -> faceplant,
  deadfallknee -> stumblefall, getup_quick_a -> getup_a).
- **Shi No Numa's Japanese zombie clips.** T5 swaps walk5-8, run4-6 and
  sprint3-4 to `ai_zombie_jap_*`. No C1 zone ships them under any name:
  - not in the 1,221 common_gametype_zm xanims, the patch zone or any zm map
    zone;
  - not in zm_sumpf_sh.animlist, whose 48 entries are the blackhole, quad
    and Thundergun sets, the magic box and the monkey bomb.
  
  Porting them would need:
  1. extracting the 13 xanims from T5's zombie_cod5_sumpf.ff;
  2. converting them to C1's xanim format (bone set and delta layout);
  3. adding them to the zm_sumpf_sh usermap fastfile (an encrypted IWffu100
     container this toolchain cannot read or write today);
  4. listing them in zm_sumpf_sh.animlist, so the C1 client and the server
     both index them;
  5. adding the WaW mapping in the Sumpf level script.
  
  Until then Sumpf keeps the standard cycles.

## Reproducing

```
# T5 (Plutonium installed; copy tools/t5cap/zz_t5cap.gsc to
#   %LOCALAPPDATA%\Plutonium\storage\t5\scripts\sp\ first)
powershell -File tools\t5cap\t5run.ps1 -map zombie_cod5_prototype -extra "+set t5cap_scn r1 +set t5cap_dur 180 +set t5cap_file t5_r1.txt +set t5cap_freeze 1"
#   -> %LOCALAPPDATA%\Plutonium\storage\t5\raw\scriptdata\t5_r1.txt
# CoDOL
powershell -File tools\probe.ps1 -Port 17785 -Name r1 -Map zm_prototype_sh -Zone zm -Gametype zm -Boot 10 -Tail 220 `
  -Extra "+set g_difficulty 1 +set t5cap_scn r1 +set t5cap_dur 180 +set t5cap_bot 1 +set t5cap_freeze 1 +set t5cap_file c_r1.txt"
#   -> %TEMP%\codol-probe-r1\main\c_r1.txt
python tools/t5cap_analyze.py t5_r1.txt c_r1.txt
# T5 clip tables: scenario "dump" (+set t5cap_dogs 1 on zombie_cod5_sumpf for the hounds), then
python tools/t5_root_table.py <sumpf dump> <prototype dump>
```
